# Appeal of Denied Prior Authorization — Request for Reconsideration

**Date:** [Date this letter is sent]

**To:** [Appeals address printed on my denial letter — Texas Medicaid managed-care plan / state Medicaid agency]
**Copy to:** [Texas Health and Human Services Commission — state Medicaid agency address]

**From:**
Jordan Jennings
Member ID: W374276116
[Street address]
[City, State, ZIP]
[Phone number]

**RE: Appeal of adverse benefit determination dated 2026-08-19**
**Reference number:** POC-7B726A30C1-53854
**Service denied:** Lower back (lumbar) fusion, CPT 22612
**Plan:** Medicaid (Texas)

---

Dear Appeals Reviewer,

I am appealing the denial of the lumbar fusion surgery (CPT 22612) that my surgeon requested for me. The denial notice is dated 2026-08-19 and carries reference number POC-7B726A30C1-53854. I am asking the plan to reconsider that decision and to approve this surgery.

**A note about the criteria used to deny my request.** The notice tells me the request does not meet the plan's criteria for medical necessity and that the decision was made under the plan's applicable medical policy and clinical review criteria. However, no policy document or set of criteria was given to me with the denial, and I have not been provided with any language from the plan's criteria. For that reason, nothing in this letter is presented as a quotation from the plan. I am appealing on the facts in my medical records, which I have set out below.

**Request for the criteria in writing.** The plan holds the clinical criteria it applied to my case; I do not. I am asking the plan, in writing, to send me the clinical criteria applied to my prior authorization for CPT 22612 — the specific rule, guideline, or vendor criteria set used, including any thresholds for symptom duration, conservative treatment, imaging findings, or functional limitation that the reviewer relied on. I am sending a copy of this request to the Texas state Medicaid agency. Without those criteria, I cannot see which requirement my records were found not to meet, and I reserve the right to supplement this appeal once I receive them.

## What my records show

My surgeon, Dr. Duval, MD, of orthopedic surgery, has documented that this procedure is needed. These are the facts as they appear in the prior authorization packet:

- **Length and course of symptoms.** I have had 18 months of progressive pain in my lower back and legs. It is not relieved by rest.

- **Conservative treatment, completed and documented.** I completed supervised physical therapy including core stabilization and lumbar flexibility — 16 weeks, from 2026-04-09 to 2026-07-30, with 24 visits completed. This is documented in the physical therapy discharge note.

- **Medication and injection.** I took NSAIDs for 6 months with inadequate relief. I had a corticosteroid injection on 2026-06-19, which gave me 3 weeks of partial relief.

- **Imaging.** On 2026-07-08 I had an MRI of the lumbar spine and flexion-extension radiographs. They show grade I degenerative spondylolisthesis at L4-L5 with 5 mm of translation on flexion-extension, and severe central stenosis compressing the cauda equina.

- **Examination findings.** My exam shows neurogenic claudication and diminished sensation in both L5 dermatomes. I have no bowel or bladder dysfunction.

- **How this affects my daily life.** I cannot stand or walk more than 10 minutes before leg pain and heaviness force me to stop. Sitting relieves it.

- **Surgical risk factors.** I have no active infection and no untreated substance use. My BMI is 29 and I am a non-smoker.

## Why I am asking for reconsideration

Taken together, my records document a condition that has lasted a year and a half and has gotten worse, not better; a full course of supervised physical therapy that I completed; six months of medication and an injection that did not give me lasting relief; objective imaging showing instability on motion and severe compression of the nerves; matching findings on physical examination; and a real, measurable loss of my ability to stand and walk. My surgeon reviewed all of this and documented that the surgery is needed.

Because the plan has not told me which requirement my file was found not to meet, I am asking that the plan re-examine the complete record against whatever criteria it applied, and that it identify those criteria for me in writing. If any specific element is still considered missing, I ask that the plan state plainly what it is, so that my surgeon and I have a fair chance to supply it.

## What I am asking for

I ask the plan to overturn the denial dated 2026-08-19 and authorize the lumbar fusion (CPT 22612) requested by Dr. Duval. I also ask for a written copy of the clinical criteria applied to this request.

My appeal must be received by 2027-02-15, which is 180 days from the date of the notice. I am submitting this letter to the appeal address printed on my denial letter. I understand that Texas Medicaid appeals may also be pursued through my managed-care plan and that I may request a state fair hearing, and I intend to preserve those rights. If anything further is needed from me, please contact me at the phone number above. Please also send a copy of your decision to Dr. Duval at [surgeon's address / fax number].

Thank you for taking another look at my case.

Sincerely,

**Jordan Jennings**
Member ID: W374276116
Date of birth: [Date of birth]
[Signature]
Date: [Date]

**Enclosures:** [Copy of denial notice dated 2026-08-19] · [Physical therapy discharge note, 2026-04-09 to 2026-07-30] · [MRI and flexion-extension radiograph reports, 2026-07-08] · [Office notes from Dr. Duval] · [Injection record, 2026-06-19]

---

*This letter is not medical or legal advice and does not guarantee that coverage will be approved.*

evidence.submission_route: Medicaid is run by your state. Appeal through your state Medicaid agency or your managed-care plan, and you can also ask for a state fair hearing. All of the details are on your denial letter. By phone: the number on the back of your insurance card Deadline: Often just 30 to 90 days — act quickly and check your letter -- but your denial letter is authoritative. Use the appeal address printed on your denial letter.
evidence.criteria_request: Most state Medicaid programs publish the rules for HOW a decision must be made but not the medical criteria for a specific surgery - those usually sit with your managed-care plan or its review vendor. Ask your plan in writing for 'the clinical criteria applied to my prior authorization', and copy your state Medicaid agency. Massachusetts, North Carolina and California are the exceptions - they publish real procedure criteria.
